clue.text: See 14
Personification of English religious book

parts.note: PI is informal shorthand for pious, so religious
a tome is a large, weighty book

explanation.surface: A Bible-type volume from England held up as the embodiment of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is the perfect example of a quality is said to embody or personify it.

clue.text: Something running from baby, a leak initially

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of the word leak

explanation.surface: Something is dribbling out of an infant, starting as a small leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something running' looks like a liquid; it means a running tally.
explanation.definitionFit: A running tally of figures that keeps being added to is a sum kept up to date as you go.

clue.text: Gives in "Listener" puzzle — one torn out

indicators.note: puzzle, read as a verb, means to confuse, so the remaining letters are jumbled
torn out says a letter is ripped away from the word Listener

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone surrenders over a Listener crossword after a page is torn from the magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famously hard crossword in The Times. 'torn out' removes I (one) from LISTENER, leaving LSTENER, which 'puzzle' jumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften and yield after resisting, a synonym for giving in.

clue.text: Inclined to take Narnia lion to Tumnus, firstly

parts.note: Aslan is the lion in C. S. Lewis's Narnia books

indicators.note: firstly asks for just the opening letter of the name Tumnus

explanation.surface: A Narnia reader is keen to bring the great lion to meet the faun Tumnus first.
explanation.walkthrough: Tumnus is the faun in the same Narnia story, which makes the surface hang together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lying at a slant is tilted, or inclined, away from the vertical.

clue.text: Ruler of African country losing heart to lieutenant

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the country's name is dropped, here swapped for another piece

parts.note: Sudan is a country in north-east Africa

explanation.surface: A leader of an African nation, dispirited, hands power to a junior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of SUDAN is its central D; 'to lieutenant' says LT goes in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan is the sovereign of a Muslim state, so a ruler.

clue.text: See 26
Cezanne's Labour Party searched for reshuffle?

indicators.note: a reshuffle rearranges posts, here the letters before it

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for the Labour party in British politics

explanation.surface: The Labour Party hunting about for a cabinet reshuffle, with a nod to Cezanne.
explanation.walkthrough: Cezanne painted a series of card-game pictures, and each answer in this puzzle is a painting named by its artist. L plus PARTY SEARCHED is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: This series of paintings of men playing cards is among Cezanne's best-known works.

clue.text: Rembrandt's basic structure encapsulated by whatever, having fewer clothes

indicators.note: encapsulated by says the piece is enclosed inside the following word

parts.note: any, as in 'any one at all', means whatever
an atom is the basic structural unit of matter
someone with fewer clothes has less on

explanation.surface: Rembrandt's picture of a basic body somehow shown with less clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Rembrandt painted a famous dissection scene of Dr Tulp lecturing; 'whatever' as ANY is a stretch but sound, as in 'any book will do'.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1632 group portrait of a surgeon dissecting a corpse is one of Rembrandt's masterpieces.

clue.text: Device inside which awful if trapped?

indicators.note: inside points to letters sitting within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A machine in which it would be dreadful to be stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures being stuck in an elevator, which is exactly what the device is; the letters straddle awful, if and trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevator is a mechanical device for carrying people between floors.

clue.text: Women letting new boys go around with decapitated kippers

indicators.note: go around says the first boy encircles the following letter

parts.note: two boys, each a lad

indicators.note: decapitated means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: kippers are kipper ties, the wide 1970s neckties

explanation.surface: Landlords' wives letting youngsters wander about carrying fish with their heads cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kippers' looks like fish but means kipper ties, the wide 1970s fashion; 'decapitated' leaves IES, and 'go around' puts N inside the first of two lads.
explanation.definitionFit: Landladies are women who let rooms or property to tenants.

clue.text: Toulouse-Lautrec's filmed sex symbol virtually captures Miss Andrews' heart with headless mammoth

indicators.note: captures says the cut-down name holds the next piece inside it
virtually means almost all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Marilyn Monroe was Hollywood's best-known screen sex symbol

indicators.note: heart keeps only the middle of the name, losing its first and last letters

parts.note: Julie Andrews is the actress and singer

indicators.note: headless removes the opening letter

parts.note: mammoth means huge

explanation.surface: Toulouse-Lautrec's screen siren holds the heart of Julie Andrews and a beheaded woolly beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' trims the actress's surname by its last letter, and 'heart' keeps the middle three letters of Julie; 'captures' sets those inside the shortened surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris cabaret and its dancers were the subject of many of Toulouse-Lautrec's posters and paintings.

clue.text: Delinquent offered non-alcoholic drink's bloody angry, extremely!

parts.note: tea is a drink with no alcohol
raw meat is bloody and uncooked

indicators.note: extremely asks for the outermost letters of the word angry

explanation.surface: A young hoodlum handed a soft drink turns furiously cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a reckless, unruly youngster, a juvenile delinquent.

clue.text: Paul's about to compile, going back into business for very little money abroad

indicators.note: into says the reversed piece is placed within the business abbreviation

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: going back means the combined letters are read in reverse
about says the setter's word goes round the next piece

parts.note: Paul is the setter, so Paul's is mine
to set a crossword is to compile it

explanation.surface: The setter, about to put a puzzle together, returns to work for a pittance overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves, so Paul's is 'mine'; 'about' wraps it round SET, 'going back' gives ENTESIM, and 'into' places that within the business abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The centesimo was a hundredth of an Italian lira, so a tiny unit of foreign currency.

clue.text: Van Gogh's hope shattered thanks to drug being absorbed by his subjects' meal?

indicators.note: being absorbed by says everything before it goes inside the meal that follows

parts.note: taters is informal for potatoes, the peasants' supper in the painting

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so all the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Van Gogh's optimism dashed as narcotics are soaked up by the food his sitters eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' turns HOPE into HEPO; the meal is informal 'taters', potatoes, and its first letter T is split from the rest by the absorbed run. The painting shows peasants at supper.
explanation.definitionFit: This dark 1885 canvas of a peasant family at supper is one of Van Gogh's key early paintings.

clue.text: Slough residence for rakes?

definitions.meaning: to slough is to cast off, as a snake does its skin
a garden outbuilding where tools such as rakes are kept, rakes playing on dissolute men

explanation.definitionFit: To cast off skin is to slough it; a garden hut houses the rakes.

clue.text: Masticate, or repeat audibly for training?

definitions.meaning: to masticate is to grind food with the teeth
the word said twice sounds like choo-choo, a child's word for a train

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: say the word twice and it sounds like a steam train, 'training' being a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Masticating food means grinding it between the teeth, which is what chomping does.

clue.text: Line turning up around slum to acquire disease

indicators.note: around says the reversed line encloses the next piece
turning up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an arc is a curved line
a hole is a squalid dwelling, a slum

explanation.surface: A row of slum dwellings ends up spreading an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is an acute intestinal infection spread through dirty water.

clue.text: Fielder right in deep about to be beaten

parts.note: slip is a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper

indicators.note: about means the combined letters are turned round
in says one letter sits within the next word

parts.note: the deep is the outfield near the boundary in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer posted on the boundary is about to be hammered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives DEREP, and 'about' turns that to PERED. To be slippered was to be beaten with a slipper, an old school punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being slippered was a schoolboy punishment, beaten on the backside with a slipper.

clue.text: See 7
Resolute scorer in cricket match dismissing opener

indicators.note: in says the composer's name goes inside the shortened match
dismissing opener drops the first letter, a cricket pun on sending a batsman out

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
Thomas Arne was the English composer who scored Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A determined batsman piling on runs in a Test while the opening batter is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' wants to be a run-maker, but it is a writer of musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Being earnest means being serious and determined in purpose, so resolute.

clue.text: A grand in addition

parts.note: swell is an old-fashioned word for fine or grand

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like a thousand pounds but means splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means also or besides, adding something further.

clue.text: Goya's bereavement accommodated by homeless relative

indicators.note: accommodated by means housed within the following word
homeless drops the letters meaning at home, 'in'

parts.note: a cousin is a relative
a bereavement is the loss of a loved one

explanation.surface: A grieving Goya figure is taken in by a relation who has no house.
explanation.walkthrough: IN means at home, so 'homeless' cuts COUSIN to COUS, which holds LOSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Goya's dark painting of a giant striding above a fleeing crowd bears this title.

clue.text: Reni's "A Lion is Heard"

indicators.note: is Heard signals that the phrase is spoken and the answer is what it sounds like

parts.note: a lion is a roarer, so the phrase is a roarer

explanation.surface: Reni's painting of a lion as if it were a title of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Guido Reni painted the dawn goddess on a Rome ceiling. Said in a non-rhotic British accent, 'a roarer' matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Guido Reni's celebrated ceiling fresco in Rome shows the goddess of the dawn.

clue.text: See 11
To understand about alcoholics having turned over notice outside hen party is a deep thing

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round what follows

parts.note: to see is to understand
AA is Alcoholics Anonymous

indicators.note: having turned over says the notice's words are read backwards

parts.note: a sign on the door of a women-only party would read no men

explanation.surface: Grasping the drinkers' plight after reversing the sign on a bachelorette bash is profound.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is a British pre-wedding party for the bride and her female friends.
explanation.definitionFit: This marine animal lives on the seabed, so it is something found in the deep.

clue.text: Guardian editor exploited

parts.note: the Guardian newspaper, where this puzzle ran, refers to itself as us

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editor has been taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: Something used has been taken advantage of or employed for a purpose, so exploited.

clue.text: Bernini's "Poland" copied — a fake, and he too!

indicators.note: fake means counterfeit, so the letters are reworked
copied means the word appears twice

parts.note: the country's name taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Bernini sculpture faked in Poland, with the artist himself in on the forgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Bernini's marble shows a nymph turning into a laurel as a god chases her. POLAND POLAND plus A and HE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This marble group of a god pursuing a nymph is one of Bernini's most famous sculptures.

clue.text: Seal of approval given on condition when delivered

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
something sent has been delivered

explanation.surface: Approval is granted only if goods arrive in the state they were dispatched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given on condition' simply joins; read together, the pieces say 'as sent', the state goods are in on delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is formal agreement or approval, such as royal assent to a bill.
